pages.text: Spring flowers opened wide in a forest clearing. Yellow, white, pink. Every breeze carried their scent.
Nils wanted a bouquet for the cabin table. "I'll take all the pretty flowers!"
He began picking. One hand full, then the other.
Even his arms weren't enough. He tucked flowers under his chin too.
Still, the flowers over there looked prettier. Nils bent to pick more.
Tumble! Flowers spilled from his arms. As he picked them up, more spilled.
The stems in his hands were crumpled. The flowers hung their heads.
Grandpa picked up three flowers. "Take only as many flowers as your hand can hold."
Nils chose just five. They fitted in one hand, fresh and lively.
The bouquet stood in a vase on the table. The cabin brightened. Nils smiled. "Just right!"
